research_question: Does combining TLS fingerprint information, including JA3 and JA4 where available, with encrypted-flow behavioral features improve malicious encrypted-traffic detection compared with individual feature families, under realistic generalization conditions and without decrypting TLS application payloads?

known_limitations: Labels are capture-level and propagated to every flow; benign background traffic inside malware captures is labelled MALICIOUS.
Each dataset contributes exactly one class (DS-008, DS-009 malicious; DS-011, DS-004 benign), so dataset identity and label are perfectly aligned at the source level.
DS-011 benign traffic is 2017 browser traffic (iceweasel 43 / Firefox-era stacks) to popular sites; it is not representative of enterprise or modern client traffic.
DS-008 captures are from 2024-2026 while DS-009/DS-011 are from 2017: TLS versions and client stacks differ systematically by year.
ClientHello parsing uses the first TCP segment only; fingerprints from truncated records are flagged (clienthello_record_truncated).
DS-004 (CipherSpectrum) is absent from this working copy and is therefore not part of the corpus.

sufficiency.interpretation: Levels are cumulative requirements for increasingly strong claims. Meeting A or B permits executing and reporting preliminary, explicitly confounded results; it does not support generalisation claims (C) or publication claims (D).

availability_asymmetry.note: When fingerprint availability differs strongly between classes, presence flags and missingness carry label information on their own; see the P_AVAILABILITY_PROBE results.

A_FLOW.description: Flow behaviour + TLS structural metadata (no fingerprints)

A_FLOW@JA3POP.description: Track A features on the JA3-available population (paired contrast with D)

A_FLOW@JA4POP.description: Track A features on the JA4-available population (paired contrast with E)

A0_FLOW_STRICT.description: Flow behaviour only, without TLS structural metadata (ablation)

P_AVAILABILITY_PROBE.description: Shortcut probe: handshake presence / availability flags only

pooled_capture_cv.description: All admitted captures; whole capture sessions held out (stratified group 5-fold).

matched_lab_capture_cv.description: Least-confounded subset: DS-009 malware and DS-011 benign captures from the same laboratory and period.

leave_one_source_out.description: Each dataset held out in turn; single-class test folds report detection rate or false-positive rate.

leave_one_family_out.description: Each malware family group held out with one rotating benign capture.

legacy_behavioral_holdout.description: Phase 7 protocol (GroupShuffleSplit on behavioral_hash, seed 42) for continuity; captures leak across sides.

encoding_ablation.description: Fingerprint encoding strategies (one-hot, train-frequency, hashing) under capture-grouped CV.

source_identifiability.description: Diagnostic, not detection: can features tell the two MALICIOUS sources (DS-008 vs DS-009) apart?

confirmatory_policy.rule: A confirmatory evaluation must use at least one benign and one malicious source that were never used in any exploratory run, evaluated once with a configuration frozen in advance.
confirmatory_policy.reason: All currently admitted sources (DS-008, DS-009, DS-011) are used in exploratory suites.

dummy_prior.description: Predicts the training prevalence; the floor every model must beat.

extra_trees.description: Extremely randomised trees (150 trees), balanced weights.

hist_gb.description: Histogram gradient boosting (100 iterations), balanced weights. Benchmark only (not exportable).

claims.claim: The system does not decrypt TLS application payloads.
claims.evidence_summary: Only TLS handshake records (ClientHello/ServerHello) in the first segment are parsed; packet payloads are otherwise reduced to sizes, timings, directions and TCP flags. No key material, interception or decryption code exists (pipeline/tls_fingerprinting.py, backend/event_sources/live_capture.py). The Zeek, Suricata and eBPF adapters read only metadata fields logged by those tools (backend/event_sources/{zeek,suricata,ebpf}_source.py).

claims.claim: The Zeek, Suricata and eBPF adapters normalise records into the canonical flow contract without fabricating fingerprints, endpoints, protocols, durations or rates, and without silently dropping, duplicating or relabelling records.
claims.evidence_summary: pipeline/canonical_flow.py; tests/test_canonical_flow.py, tests/test_sensors_zeek.py, tests/test_sensors_suricata.py, tests/test_sensors_ebpf.py (placeholder fingerprints rejected, negotiated TLS version / selected ALPN kept apart from ETTH features, expiry and overflow emit instead of drop, duplicates and late records counted).
limitations: Verified with synthetic fixtures only; no real Zeek, Suricata or eBPF collector output was processed.
Software contract evidence, not detection-quality evidence.

claims.claim: Models trained on ETTH packet features and ETTH JA4 refuse sensor-aggregate statistics and FoxIO JA4 instead of scoring them.
claims.evidence_summary: backend/inference_engine.py provenance and JA4-implementation rules; tests/test_inference_contract.py (FoxIO reference ClientHello: ETTH JA4 t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_0adf69b4533f vs FoxIO ..._e5627efa2ab1) and tests/test_cross_phase_integration.py (all five tracks on sensor fixtures).
limitations: Verified with synthetic fixtures only; no real Zeek, Suricata or eBPF collector output was processed.
Software contract evidence, not detection-quality evidence.

claims.claim: Live capture produces the same flows (boundaries, initiator direction) and the same flow and TLS feature values as the offline PCAP pipeline for the same packets.
claims.evidence_summary: tests/test_live_offline_parity.py: synthetic packets written to a PCAP give identical flows and FLOW features (rel/abs 1e-9) through pipeline.flow_reconstruction and LiveCaptureSource.
limitations: Native capture was not exercised (no capture driver on the integration host).
Flows longer than the live maximum duration are split, flagged and refused by flow-feature models.

claims.claim: ETTH detection models can score flows observed by Zeek, Suricata or eBPF sensors.
claims.evidence_summary: No model is trained on sensor-observable features with sensor provenance, and no labelled sensor telemetry is available. Under the current contract only the JA3-only track accepts sensor flows, and those JA3 values are mostly outside the training vocabulary (UNSEEN_CATEGORY).
